thread.title: The Amazon chart you may not want to see, but probably should

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: The Amazon chart you may not want to see, but probably should
text:
Welcome to big game day — the “Super Bowl of Earnings,” as some are calling it.
Apple, Amazon and Alphabet are getting ready to dazzle us (or not) with results after the close. Already out there are reports from Facebook, Microsoft, Qualcomm and PayPal, all likely to grab some post-earnings spotlight this morning.
Oh, and 10-year bond yields are creeping up again, so fix a third eye on that.
Read: Ready to rock the market: Six tech companies worth a collective $500 billion
On a potentially manic day like this, it’s good to focus on just one thing. That brings us to our chart of the day from Jesse Felder of the Felder Report , who offers this revenue picture for one of the big three — Amazon.
The chart compares Amazon’s enterprise-value-to-revenue multiple, or EV/R (shown in blue) with the e-commerce giant’s five-year revenue growth (shown in red). EV/R is one way of measuring whether investors may be paying too much for a stock — you want the ratio to go down, not up.
And that’s exactly what’s not happening, going by this chart. On top of that, the red, stair-stepped area shows Amazon’s revenue growth is the weakest it’s been in a decade.
Amazon’s share gain of 25% over the past 31 days — with another record close Wednesday — equals a $143.78 billion market-cap gain , Felder notes. In other words, it added a McDonald’s MCD, +0.53% in market cap in the month of January, given the burger chain is at $136.4 billion.
What this all might mean is that investors are willing to buy growth at any cost, says Felder. When it comes to Amazon, though, those fans may be ignoring the risk of regulatory action ahead, that could cut into revenue. ( In health care , perhaps?)
“Regardless, at some point the market will return to being a weighing machine, and today’s euphoric votes on the part of investors might look silly in retrospect,” says the investment letter writer.
That said, Amazon has been a phenomenal stock, growing from under $40 during the financial crisis to Wednesday’s $1,450 record, and no doubt has boosted some retirement funds. But amid the feverish chatter about its earnings — and even talk of a stock split — it’s worth pondering how much further shares will go.
Wow chart! #Amazon , already one of the biggest companies on earth, is up a staggering 50% since it’s Q3 earnings report! pic.twitter.com/WwwletvKTe
— jeroen blokland (@jsblokland) January 31, 2018 And there’s no doubt it’s got clout. Amazon is now the world’s most valuable brand, up 42% in a year to beat Google and Apple to the top, according to Brand Finance’s Global 500 study .
“All evidence suggests that the amazing Amazon brand is going to continue growing indefinitely and exponentially," said David Haigh, CEO of Brand Finance, in the report. Well, there is that.
Market snapshot A weaker start is undeway, with the Dow DJIA, -0.03% , S&P 500 SPX, -0.12% and Nasdaq COMP, -0.28% all in the red. Maybe look to Europe SXXP, -0.50% where the DAX DAX, -1.41% is slumping on rising bond yields.
Chinese stocks SHCOMP, -0.97% plunged 3% on flat factory data, though the Nikkei NIK, +1.68% rose.
The dollar DXY, -0.37% is off a bit, largely against the euro EURUSD, +0.6928% Gold GCH8, +0.34% is flat, and crude CLH8, +1.30% is up 1%. The yield on the 10-year Treasury TMUBMUSD10Y, +2.36% is up to 2.725%.
See the Market Snapshot column for the latest action.
Bitcoin BTCUSD, -11.42% is dropping fairly hard , and is now well under $10,000.
The buzz Did this week’s two-day pullback for stocks have you reaching for the eject button? Keep calm and hold on, says our call of the day , from Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA.
“Even though the S&P 500 has pulled back from its recent highs, its bias remains bullish,” writes Stovall in a note to clients.
He says the “uptrend” remains in place for the S&P 500. Only breaches of the established support levels at 2,798 and then 2,736 would “suggest to us that the continuing rally is changing its upward trajectory,” Stovall adds.
The Quote: “This is going change our lives, to tell you the truth.” — That was 51-year old Donald Savastano from Queens, New York, shortly after winning the state’s “Merry Millionaire” lottery game, and not long before he died.
The first stop for the self-employed and uninsured carpenter was a doctor’s appointment, as he’d been feeling unwell for a while. Diagnosed with stage 4 cancer, Savastano passed away on Friday, 23 days after striking it lucky.

The buzz EBay EBAY, +14.14% is up about 10% after earnings. The online auctioneer also announced a further split with PayPal PYPL, -7.04% , whose shares are going the other way after its own results beat forecasts.
Facebook FB, +3.31% is up after results, where it revealed double-digit ad-price growth .
Not much movement for Microsoft MSFT, -1.02% , which posted a tax-cut-related loss . But CEO Satya Nadella seems to know what he’s doing right now .
Qualcomm QCOM, -1.79% got hit with a $6 billion quarterly loss . And its disclosure that a big customer cut orders more than expected in the quarter initially jarred Apple AAPL, -0.05% . Some think that revelation is further proof that Apple curtailed iPhone X production sooner than thought.
Read: Apple should have marketed the iPhone X like a gourmet jam
We’ll find out the deal when Apple reports after the close , along with Amazon and Alphabet
Alibaba BABA, -5.71% is down on a holiday-earnings miss, Boston Scientific BSX, -1.45% Time Warner TWX, +1.67% and ConocoPhillips COP, +0.51% also reported. Amgen AMGN, -0.49% , Visa V, +0.40% , Mattel MAT, -1.96% and GoPro GPRO, -0.91% GPRO, -0.91% will report after the close.
AT&T T, +4.15% is moving higher after a $20 billion paper gain.
Tesla TSLA, -1.18% CEO Elon Musk says they’ve sold out of flamethrowers — all 20,000.
Flamethrowers sold out
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) February 1, 2018 Nintendo 7974, +0.52% up 106% over the last 12 months, put out a trifecta of announcements, including on the launch of an online subscription service.
Data may have stressed out markets a bit. Productivity dipped in the fourth quarter , and weekly jobless claims fell just slightly. The Markit manufacturing PMI, ISM manufacturing, construction spending and auto sales are headed our way.
The battle royale over the GOP memo took a new twist after Rep. Adam Schiff accused Republicans of sneakily switching out the report approved by the House Intelligence Committee for different version.
